metaDescription: Six countertop microwaves listed at or below $150, from a humidity sensor model to retro and stainless units, compared on wattage, capacity and extras.
expertTake: The TOSHIBA 1.2 is the top pick for a humidity sensor, 1000 W and a 12.4 inch turntable. The BLACK+DECKER 1.1 is the value pick for a plain 1000 W unit. Skip the retro model unless style matters more than watts.
introParagraphs: The extra budget over the basic tier buys a bigger cavity, a sensor or a design finish. It rarely buys faster cooking, because 1000 W is already the practical sweet spot.

This guide looks at where the extra money goes. We favour units that spend it on capacity and a sensor over those that spend it only on looks. Check turntable diameter and dimensions against your counter, since the larger units here need noticeably more room than the 0.7 cubic foot class, and that a retro or stainless case adds no cooking performance. Prices move, so the $150 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: TOSHIBA countertop microwave 1.2 cu ft, 1000 W, humidity sensor
products.description:
The TOSHIBA 1.2 delivers 1000 W output on 1600 W input, with a smart humidity sensor, twelve auto menus and a mute function. Its turntable is 12.4 inches and removable, which fits a standard dinner plate. External dimensions are 20.6 by 14.6 by 11.8 inches.

The sensor adjusts time and power by food humidity, which saves guesswork. It is the largest cavity here. Its humidity sensor and 1.2 cu ft beat the plain 1.1 cu ft units.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and take out the turntable to wash it. Before relying on the TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave for a week of meals, run a cup of water for one minute and check how hot it gets, then adjust package times to its wattage.
products.bestFor: Families who want a sensor and a large cavity

products.name: BLACK+DECKER countertop microwave 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W, child safety
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER 1.1 gives 1000 W in a 1.1 cubic foot cavity with six one touch presets and a child safety lock. Its dimensions are 20.6 by 16.5 by 11.8 inches. The listing calls it large capacity but compact.

It is a clear step up from the 0.9 unit in capacity and power. It is a straightforward family microwave. Its 1000 W and 1.1 cu ft are plainer than the TOSHIBA.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Place the BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave with clear space around it and a stable, level surface, since blocked vents and an uneven turntable are common causes of poor results.
products.bestFor: Families who want a plain 1000 W unit

products.name: Chefman countertop microwave 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W, 10 power levels
products.description:
The Chefman 1.1 is a 1000 W digital microwave with ten power levels and six one touch presets. It offers express cooking buttons. It packs a family size cavity into a plain body.

It is the near match to the BLACK+DECKER 1.1. Choose on the look and the preset list. It is a near match to the BLACK+DECKER 1.1 with a different panel.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Use microwave safe containers in the Chefman 1.1 microwave and stir food halfway, because cold spots are normal in any model at this price.
products.bestFor: Families who want a digital 1000 W unit

products.name: Farberware countertop microwave 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W
products.description:
The Farberware 1.1 is a 1000 W microwave with ten power levels and multi stage cooking. It has six preset buttons and a stainless steel finish. It hits the wattage sweet spot for full meals.

At 1.1 cubic feet it holds a standard dinner plate. It is a good value family size. Its multi stage cooking and stainless finish suit a family.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Wipe the cavity of the Farberware 1.1 microwave after spatters, as baked on residue spreads odours and can cause arcing near the waveguide cover.
products.bestFor: Families who want 1000 W at a modest size

products.name: Chefman 0.9 cu ft digital stainless microwave, 900 W, eco mode
products.description:
The Chefman 0.9 stainless is a 900 W digital microwave with ten power levels, six presets, an eco mode and a mute function. The stainless steel finish matches modern appliances. It is the dressier sibling of the plain Chefman.

The eco mode trims standby power. It suits kitchens with stainless appliances. Its eco mode and stainless finish sit at 900 W, below the 1000 W units.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Keep the manual for the Chefman 0.9 stainless microwave, since the child lock and mute sequences differ between brands and are easy to trigger by accident.

products.name: Nostalgia retro countertop microwave 0.9 cu ft, 800 W
products.description:
The Nostalgia retro microwave offers 800 W in a 0.9 cubic foot cavity with twelve pre programmed cooking settings, a delay timer and express cooking. It is styled in a retro look. It is a design led pick.

At 800 W it sits between the 700 W and 900 W units. The twelve presets are more than most rivals. Its retro look and twelve presets come at 800 W, the lowest power here.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Do not run the Nostalgia retro microwave empty or with metal or foil inside, because both can damage the magnetron or cause arcing.
cons: 800 W is below the 900 W units
Style costs more than a plain unit

buyingCriteria.explanation: Mechanical dials last long with little to fail, while digital panels add presets and a clock. A dial is simple to use and cheap to make, and a digital panel suits people who want popcorn and potato buttons. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave (1.1 cu ft, 1000 W) and Farberware 1.1 microwave (1.1 cu ft, 1000 W) sit on different sides. Choose the control style you will use daily.

Ten power levels and a defrost by weight or time let you thaw without cooking the edges. Cheaper microwaves pulse full power on and off, which is harsh on frozen food. TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave and Chefman 1.1 microwave offer different presets. Use lower power and stir or rest food to even out the heat.

Cubic feet is a weaker guide than turntable diameter, since a 12.4 inch turntable fits a standard dinner plate and a smaller one may not. Small microwaves run about 0.5 to 0.9 cubic feet, midsize 1.1 to 1.7 and large 1.7 to 2.2. TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave and Chefman 1.1 microwave differ in capacity in this lineup. Measure your biggest plate before you buy.

The beep after a cycle can be loud, and a mute option fixes that for night use. Eco modes cut standby power by dimming the display. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave and Farberware 1.1 microwave are worth comparing on those details. These are small things that matter in a small apartment.

A microwave needs space on the sides and top for its vents, and a unit jammed into a tight shelf runs hot. Compact units give up cavity for footprint. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave and Farberware 1.1 microwave show the size spread in this lineup. Measure the counter and the clearance before ordering.

A one year warranty is typical, and the magnetron and the door latch are the usual failure points. A cheap unit is often cheaper to replace than to repair. TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave and Chefman 1.1 microwave are covered by the standard period. Keep the receipt and register the product.

specDecoder.meaning: The glass plate that rotates food. About 12.4 inches fits a standard dinner plate.
specDecoder.watchFor: See whether Farberware 1.1 microwave states a diameter.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of steps between low and full power. Ten levels give finer control for defrosting.
specDecoder.watchFor: Note which of TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave and BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave gives ten levels.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the cavity. Small is about 0.5 to 0.9, midsize 1.1 to 1.7 and large 1.7 to 2.2.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check how Chefman 1.1 microwave states its cavity and turntable size.

specDecoder.meaning: Output watts describe how much microwave energy reaches the food. Input power is higher, and the label times assume the output rating.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave with BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave on output watts, not input watts.

specDecoder.meaning: A button that starts 30 seconds at full power and adds 30 seconds on each press. It is the most used button on many units.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check whether Farberware 1.1 microwave offers it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and presets
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dial versus digital controls, preset lists and power levels. We favoured units whose controls match their price. Chefman 1.1 microwave and Farberware 1.1 microwave represent different approaches in the lineup.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for child lock, mute and a pull or push door. These small features matter in busy households. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave was compared against the others on this point.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at what owners repeatedly report, not at any one summary figure. Repeated complaints about noise, door latches or uneven heating lowered a pick. This guide quotes no star figures or review totals, and no such number fed the ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wattage and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated wattage and cavity size, using the rule that about 1000 to 1250 W suits meals. We ranked how well each unit matched a household. TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave at 1.2 cu ft, 1000 W sensor and BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave at 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W were compared this way.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and placement
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at footprint, turntable size and ventilation notes. A unit that fits a counter and a plate gets used. TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave was the reference for a different size class.

howToChoose.intro: Decide first how much counter and cabinet space you can spare, since a microwave also needs ventilation clearance. Then decide whether you reheat leftovers or actually cook. The rows below map common situations to the picks in this lineup, including BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave.

rows: You want a sensor and a big cavity
You want a digital 1000 W unit

howToChoose.note: Whichever you choose, measure the space including ventilation clearance, and check that your biggest plate actually turns inside the cavity.

howToChoose.intro: Every pick here is listed at or below the $150 cap, so the tiers below are relative to each other, not to the cap.

rows: Spending the least this lineup allows
BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave (1.1 cu ft, 1000 W) costs the least in this lineup, so it suits a buyer who wants reheating and little else.
Chefman 0.9 stainless microwave (0.9 cu ft, 900 W steel) sits mid lineup on cost, balancing power, capacity and controls.
TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave (1.2 cu ft, 1000 W sensor) costs the most in this lineup, so it needs to earn that premium on wattage, capacity or features.

howToChoose.note: Treat the tiers as relative: the cheapest pick suits reheating, the middle suits everyday cooking and the top of the lineup suits families.

cards.label: Digital controls and presets
cards.text: The group of TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave, BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave, Chefman 1.1 microwave, Farberware 1.1 microwave, Chefman 0.9 stainless microwave, and Nostalgia retro microwave uses a digital panel with presets. It offers popcorn, potato and beverage buttons, a clock and a timer. It suits people who like one touch cooking.

cards.label: Dial or simple controls
cards.text: Every pick here is digital, so TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave is the closest alternative. A dial is cheap, long lasting and easy to use. It suits people who set a time and walk away.

howToChoose.note: Pick digital if you use presets daily. Pick a dial or simple panel if you want something that will not confuse anyone in the house.

rows: You cook for two and want 900 W without a large footprint
Chefman 0.9 stainless microwave and Nostalgia retro microwave
A 0.9 cubic foot unit at 900 W is the practical middle: fast enough for meals and still compact.
You cook for a family and use full size plates and dishes
TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave, BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave, Chefman 1.1 microwave, and Farberware 1.1 microwave
A 1.1 cubic foot or larger unit at 1000 W or more fits a standard dinner plate and cooks faster and more evenly than a small one.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for at least 900 W, a turntable that clears your biggest plate, a quick express button and a mute option. Ten power levels help with defrost. Those features matter more than a long preset list.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave is the pick that best matches those points here, with 1.2 cu ft, 1000 W sensor. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave and Chefman 1.1 microwave are the nearest alternatives if you want a different size or a different mix of controls.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you cook for a family or want a sensor and a larger cavity. Stepping up to TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave (1.2 cu ft, 1000 W sensor) buys the wattage or size that cheaper units lack.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you reheat leftovers and drinks for one or two. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave (1.1 cu ft, 1000 W) covers the basics, and a small difference in features rarely justifies a larger premium.

maintenance.why: A worn cord is a fire risk. Replace any unit with a frayed or warm cord.
Dust and clutter block airflow and make the unit run hot. Leave space on the sides and top.

maintenance.task: Clean the door seal and latch
maintenance.why: Residue on the seal can stop the door closing fully. A clean seal also keeps the cavity sealed.
Baked on food spreads odours and can cause arcing. A damp cloth and a bowl of steam loosen most residue.
Without food to absorb energy, the magnetron can overheat. Keep a cup of water inside when testing.

faq.q: Is a bigger microwave always better?
faq.a: Not always, since a big cavity needs counter space and a large turntable. It does fit full plates, which a small unit may not. Measure your biggest plate before choosing, as the picks like Chefman 1.1 microwave show.

faq.q: Why does my food heat unevenly?
faq.a: Microwaves create hot and cold spots, which is normal. Stir food halfway, rest it for a minute and use lower power for dense items. A larger turntable helps.
Eco mode dims or turns off the display to cut standby power, which saves a little on the bill. It does not change cooking. Check whether BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave offers it.

faq.q: Do I need a mechanical dial or digital panel?
faq.a: A dial is simple and long lasting, and a digital panel adds presets and a clock. Choose what you will use. TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave and BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave show both approaches in this guide.

faq.q: How long should a microwave last?
faq.a: With care many last several years, but the magnetron and door latch are the common failures. A cheap unit is often cheaper to replace than to repair. A sturdier unit like Farberware 1.1 microwave gives a little more headroom.

faq.q: Why does this guide stop at $150?
faq.a: The $150 cap is the search keyword shoppers use, and every pick here was listed at or below it when this guide was updated. BLACK+DECKER 1.1 microwave is the cheapest option in this lineup and TOSHIBA 1.2 microwave is the dearest, so the spread inside the cap is real. Prices move, so check the listing before you buy.
